prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this tunable moire platform

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: B022 as a single three-person part, with the citation restricted to what is secure, namely the prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. Four of us reached B022 independently, and the supporters agree on the wording. The decisive point for me is the kind of discovery. The Bistritzer-MacDonald model told us where to look, and nature answered with a regime nobody could have specified in detail beforehand: Mott-like insulators and superconducting domes controlled by a single geometric knob, reproduced in many laboratories and device geometries. That is a discovery of a new class of quantum matter, which I weigh above an extraordinary improvement of an existing capability, however well attributed. Maturity at about eight years is acceptable because the existence and reproducibility of the phenomena, not the pairing mechanism, is what the citation certifies. The chair's second question has my answer: the citation should make no claim about the pairing mechanism and should not say that theory predicted the correlated phases.
statement.case_against: The honest weaknesses are two. First, experimental credit: the 2018 first reports were a group effort, and Cory Dean's hBN-encapsulated devices and the groups of Young, Yacoby, Efetov and Yazdani are outside the three names. I cannot verify the author record of those papers from the material available to me, so I will not claim to have resolved the chair's first question; I can only say that the three-person rule forces a cut here and that the cut is defensible but not painless. Second, Eriksson is right that the continuum model gives flat bands and does not by itself predict the correlated phases, so the theory half of the citation is narrower than the headline suggests. If the committee finds that the experimental allocation cannot be defended, B012 is the better configuration and I would accept it without reluctance, since its attribution is cleaner and its confirmation is long settled.

responses.point: Kroll places B012 first on the grounds of a clean two-name attribution, independent confirmation at 10^-18 and no maturity risk, and treats B022 as spectacular but younger with the mechanism open.
responses.response: I agree with the facts: the lattice-clock attribution is the cleanest on the list and the performance is mature. Where we differ is the weight of those virtues against scope. A 10^-18 clock changes what can be measured, but B022 opened a regime of matter that is new, and I think the open mechanism is a question about interpretation of a secure discovery, which the citation can avoid. Kroll's own wording point actually helps both cases, and I support wording any B012 citation around the lattice architecture. My disagreement is about ranking, not about whether B012 is prize-worthy; it is, and it is my first alternative.

responses.point: Eriksson cautions that the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives flat bands but does not predict the correlated phases, and that the citation must be worded around what is established, not mechanism.
responses.response: I accept this and have tightened my own wording accordingly. The citation I now propose says that the theory predicted flat bands at a magic angle and that the experiment discovered the correlated and superconducting states, with no sentence implying that theory foresaw them. This is a more honest description of how the two halves relate and does not weaken the case, because the prediction told experimentalists where the interesting regime lay. I also share the view that waiting would settle credit and mechanism, but I do not think the settling is needed for the discovery itself.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B012 first, calls the lattice clock a single well-defined invention with the cleanest credit, and concedes she may be underweighting the pull of a very large new field.
responses.response: Her concession that B022 may be underweighted is fair, and I take her concern about trapped-ion groups and JILA team members seriously; that is a real attribution cost for B012 that parallels the Dean cost for B022. Where I disagree is the discovery-or-invention framing. The lattice clock is a well-defined invention, but the committee has more latitude to distinguish a new phenomenon from an improved tool, and the pending redefinition of the second means part of its value is still prospective, as she herself notes. I do not see the pending redefinition as a reason to wait or as a decisive argument for it.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B012 for its originator-level attribution and maturity, but acknowledges that B022 has broader support, a cleaner theory-then-experiment arc and arguably larger reach, with her reservation limited to experimental attribution and the field's youth.
responses.response: Her reservation about B022 is precisely the one I regard as its main weakness, so we agree on the diagnosis and differ only on the weight. She says the committee asks who is responsible for the original work and that B012 has a short answer. For B022 the answer is longer but still bounded: the prediction is Bistritzer and MacDonald, and the first observation of the correlated phases is Jarillo-Herrero's group. The long tail of later contributors is a feature of any field that has grown, and I do not think it should bar the first discoverers. I would welcome the chair's check of the first-author record before the vote.

responses.point: Johansson moved from B038 to B012, and ranks B022 only sixth because of maturity and the unsettled superconducting mechanism, while noting the pending SI redefinition.
responses.response: I understand the maturity caution, but the precedent we have is of recognising secure phenomena before their microscopic explanation is complete. I also note that he now asks whether the SI redefinition must happen before B012 is awarded; if redefinition is a legitimate wait condition for B012, then mechanism cannot be a wait condition for B022 without inconsistency, and I would rather apply neither. His withdrawal of B038 for attribution reasons seems right to me and I do not see a route to restoring it.

responses.point: Pearce, the chair, moved from B013 to B022 and asks that the author record of the first reports be examined before final votes.
responses.response: I welcome his support and his request. I would add that the examination should focus on a narrow question: whether the experimental credit for the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity can be given to Jarillo-Herrero alone without misdescribing who did the work, since the first author's role and Dean's group contributions are the relevant facts. If that examination leaves the credit unclear, the committee should say so openly and consider B012. On a two-part configuration, I agree with his report that no split of three people between B022 and B012 is fair to both sets of names.

uncertainties: Whether the experimental credit for the 2018 discovery can be fairly limited to Jarillo-Herrero, given the first author, Dean's hBN devices and the early reproductions by other groups; I cannot verify this from the material available to me.

Whether the committee treats the unresolved superconducting mechanism as a maturity problem or only as an open follow-up question, and whether that standard is applied symmetrically to the pending SI redefinition for B012.
How a committee should weigh a new regime of quantum matter (B022) against a precision-measurement invention (B012) when cleaner attribution and breadth of impact conflict.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My research is in string theory, quantum gravity and cosmology, and my documented connections (David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theoretical-physics group) do not link me to any shortlisted candidate. My second alternative, B027, reflects a disciplinary preference as a black-hole theorist and not a personal connection. I do not need recusal on B022 or B012.
